questions.stem: Suppose the university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on how to enrich students' knowledge of traditional Chinese culture. You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
Traditional Chinese culture is a treasure that shapes our national identity, yet many students today know little about it. As a contributor to our university newspaper, I would like to share several practical ways to enrich students' understanding of this precious heritage.

To begin with, our university could offer optional courses and regular lectures on classical literature, calligraphy and traditional festivals, so as to build a solid foundation of knowledge. In addition, hands-on activities are equally important. By organizing cultural experiences such as paper-cutting workshops or tea ceremonies, students can feel the charm of tradition rather than merely reading about it. Moreover, we can make full use of new media, posting short videos and articles online to spread cultural knowledge in a way that appeals to young people.

In conclusion, combining formal learning, personal experience and modern technology would help students appreciate traditional Chinese culture far more deeply. I sincerely hope these suggestions will benefit us all.

sections.title: Section II Listening Comprehension
sections.note: 听力为历年真题原文，题目与答案为官方标准答案；在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: 1 U.S. families are looking to the winter with fear as energy costs soar.
A number of factors are creating a bad situation: Global energy consumption is up, but supplies have been reduced.
The Energy Department projects heating bills will jump 28% this winter for those who rely on natural gas.
Natural gas is used by nearly half of U.S. households for heat.
Heating oil is projected to be 27% higher and electricity 10% higher.
That comes against inflation rates that accelerated last month with consumer prices growing 6.6%.
That's the fastest pace in four decades. 2 The pain will be especially acute in parts of the country that heavily rely on heating oil to keep homes warm.
It's projected to cost more than $2,300 to heat a typical home with heating oil this winter.
Last month, the federal government added $1 billion in funding to Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, bringing the total to $4.8 billion.
But that represents a reduction from last year's energy assistance package of over $8 billion.

questions.stem: Why are families across the U.S. looking to this winter with fear?

options.text: They will see a 27% higher price to buy natural gas.
They will have insufficient heating oil to keep warm.
They will have a costly bill to pay to heat their homes.
They will experience the coldest winter in four decades.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：U.S. families are looking to the winter with fear as energy costs soar. The Energy Department projects heating bills will jump 28% this winter for those who rely on natural gas.信号：as 引出发愁的直接原因 。原文 looking to the winter with fear as energy costs soar 中的 as 直接把‘发愁’与‘能源成本飙升’扣在一起，as 后面就是答案信号…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：原文确实念了 27%，但 Heating oil is projected to be 27% higher 说的是‘取暖用油’涨 27%；选项 a 27% higher price to buy natural gas 把 27% 安到了天然气头上（天然气其实是涨 28%），数字盗用且对错对象。 借用原文：supplies have been reduced
optionAnalysis.B: 过度推断：原文有 supplies have been reduced（供应减少）和大量 heating oil 字样，选项 insufficient heating oil to keep warm 借这些词造出‘油不够保暖’的说法，但原文讲的是‘费用贵’，从未说会‘缺油到取不了暖’。 借用原文：That's the fastest pace in four decades
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：原文 four decades 出现在 consumer prices growing 6.6%. That's the fastest pace in four decades，说的是‘物价涨速四十年最快’；选项 the coldest winter in four decades 却把 four decades 挪去形容‘四十年最冷的冬天’，原文根本没谈天气冷暖。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（heating bills will jump 28% ↔ a costly bill to pay to heat their homes ‘账单涨28%’概括为‘贵账单’）

questions.evidenceText: U.S. families are looking to the winter with fear as energy costs soar. The Energy Department projects heating bills will jump 28% this winter for those who rely on natural gas.

questions.stem: What did the federal government do last month?

options.text: Provided additional funding to Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program.
Assured U.S. citizens of an increase in energy supplies by the end of this year.
Predicted a 10% jump in heating bills for most U.S. households this winter.
Decided on this year's energy assistance package of $8 billion in total.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：Last month, the federal government added $1 billion in funding to Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, bringing the total to $4.8 billion.信号：Last month 与题干同词定位 。原文 Last month, the federal government added \$1 billion in funding 开头的 Last month 与题干 la…

optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：原文出现过 supplies have been reduced（供应减少），选项 Assured U.S. citizens of an increase in energy supplies 反过来说政府‘保证能源供应会增加’，方向相反，原文也无任何‘保证’动作。 借用原文：electricity 10% higher
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：原文 10% 出自 electricity 10% higher（电费涨 10%），且作预测的是能源部不是政府这一动作主体；选项 Predicted a 10% jump in heating bills 把电费的 10% 改成‘取暖账单’、又把‘预测’这一动作安给了政府上月的作为，数字与主体双错。 借用原文：last year's energy assistance package of over \$8 billion
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：原文 a reduction from last year's energy assistance package of over \$8 billion 明说 80 亿是‘去年’援助方案、且今年比它‘减少’了；选项 Decided on this year's energy assistance package of \$8 billion in total 把去年的 80 亿说成‘今年合计敲定 80 亿’，年份与金额张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（added \$1 billion in funding to Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program ↔ Provided additional funding to Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program added funding=provided additional funding）

questions.evidenceText: Last month, the federal government added $1 billion in funding to Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, bringing the total to $4.8 billion.

transcript.text: Many Americans think they make healthy food choices, but they may be viewing their diet too optimistically. That's the main finding of a new study by researchers at the U.S. Department of Agriculture in Stoneville, Mississippi.
transcript.zh: 许多美国人认为自己做出了健康的食物选择，但他们可能对自己的饮食过于乐观了。这是美国农业部位于密西西比州Stoneville的研究人员一项新研究的主要发现。

transcript.text: The study aimed to identify disconnects between how healthily Americans think they eat and how they actually do. For the study, the researchers asked participants to rate their diet as excellent, very good, good, fair or poor. Folks also completed 24-hour food questionnaires. Then, the researchers compared answers to see how well responses to the two exercises matched up.
transcript.zh: 该研究旨在找出美国人认为自己吃得有多健康与实际情况之间的差距。在研究中，研究人员要求参与者将自己的饮食评为优秀、非常好、好、一般或差。参与者还完成了24小时食物问卷。然后，研究人员比较了答案，看两项调查的回答匹配程度如何。

transcript.text: Of more than 9,700 people, roughly 85 percent were off base when asked to rate the quality of their diet, and almost all overestimated how healthy it was. Those who rated their diet as poor tended to be far more accurate. Their rating matched that of the researchers more than nine times out of ten.
transcript.zh: 在9700多人中，大约85%的人在被要求评价自己的饮食质量时偏离了实际情况，而且几乎所有人都高估了饮食的健康程度。那些将自己的饮食评为差的人往往准确得多。他们的评价在十次中有九次以上与研究人员的评价相符。

questions.stem: What is the main finding of a new study about many Americans?

options.text: They care less about their diet now than before.
They may lack adequate knowledge of healthy food.
They may hold too optimistic a view about their diet.
They pay insufficient attention to their choice of food.

questions.analysis: 主旨题。答案句（P1）：Many Americans think they make healthy food choices, but they may be viewing their diet too optimistically. That's the main finding of a new study by researchers at the U.S. Department of Agriculture in Stoneville, Mississippi.信号：转折but+点题句That's the main finding 。答案藏在转折之后：but they may be viewing their diet too optimistically 才是真意，紧接着一句 …

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：care less about their diet now than before 说"现在比从前更不在乎饮食"，录音通篇没有"今昔对比"，更没说他们"不在乎"——恰恰相反，他们"以为"自己吃得健康。属凭空捏造的对比。
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：lack adequate knowledge of healthy food 把问题归为"缺乏健康饮食知识"，但录音说的是他们"看得太乐观"（认知偏差），不是"不懂"。盗用了 healthy food 这一原词，却把病因悄悄换掉。 借用原文：make healthy food choices
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：pay insufficient attention to their choice of food 说他们"对选食不够上心"，但录音里他们其实很在意、还自认 make healthy food choices，问题是"高估"而非"不上心"。盗用 choices 一词来制造"听到 food choices 就想选"的诱惑。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（viewing their diet too optimistically ↔ hold too optimistic a view about their diet 副词转形容词的同义改写）

questions.evidenceText: Many Americans think they make healthy food choices, but they may be viewing their diet too optimistically. That's the main finding of a new study by researchers at the U.S. Department of Agriculture in Stoneville, Mississippi.

questions.stem: Who tended to rate their diet more accurately in the survey?

options.text: Those who fully understood the rating scale.
Those who cared about food quality.
Those who rated their diet as poor.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Those who rated their diet as poor tended to be far more accurate. Their rating matched that of the researchers more than nine times out of ten.信号：题干词more accurate原句复现做信号 。题干问 more accurately，录音里 tended to be far more accurate 几乎原样出现，这处与题干高度重合的句子就是答案句；紧跟的…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：Those who finished 24-hour food questionnaires. 搬来录音 completed 24-hour food questionnaires，但那只是"所有参与者都做的一个环节"，录音从没说"填了这问卷的人评得更准"。专骗听到 24-hour 这个醒目数字就选的人。 借用原文：rate the quality of their diet
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：Those who fully understood the rating scale. 说"完全看懂评分表的人"，录音只让参与者用 excellent, very good, good, fair or poor 评级，从没区分"谁更懂评分表"，更没说这类人更准。属凭空添加。
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：Those who cared about food quality. 盗用录音 rate the quality of their diet 里的 quality 一词，编出"在乎食物质量的人"，但录音问的是评级准不准，与"在不在乎质量"无关，是借原词造的假分类。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（Those who rated their diet as poor ↔ Those who rated their diet as poor 主语整句几乎原词搬运）

questions.evidenceText: Those who rated their diet as poor tended to be far more accurate. Their rating matched that of the researchers more than nine times out of ten.

transcript.text: 1 It was a heartwarming moment that dozens of Indian rescuers rallied together to use a crane in order to save an elephant trapped at the bottom of a 20-foot well.
The massive rescue effort took place last week close to an army camp.
The elephant wandered out of the jungle and fell into the well.
The army officers heard a noise coming from the well and realized an elephant was trapped deep inside.
The officers then threw in some food for the creature and called the local forest department for help.
Video of the rescue operation shows how the team used a crane to lift up the huge animal out of the well and onto the back of a truck.
It was then taken to an examining room for evaluation of any injuries.
The elephant was kept under close supervision for a few days before it was successfully released back into the wild.

questions.stem: What does the report say dozens of Indians did last week?

options.text: They gathered together to rescue an elephant.
They heard a noise from the bottom of a well.
They found an elephant wandering around a well.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：It was a heartwarming moment that dozens of Indian rescuers rallied together to use a crane in order to save an elephant trapped at the bottom of a 20-foot well.信号：题干原话定位开头句 。题干里的 dozens of Indians 直接对应录音首句 dozens of Indian rescuers rallied together，新闻第一题答案多在开头，听到这群人"齐心协力…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：录音首句明明是 a heartwarming moment（暖心时刻），选项却写成 a heartbreaking moment（令人心碎的时刻），盗用了高度相似的 heart- 开头词把情绪极性反了过来，听到 heart 就选会中招。 借用原文：The army officers heard a noise coming from the well
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴："听到井里有声音"确实在录音里 The army officers heard a noise coming from the well，但那是"军官"听到的，不是这群营救人员做的，选项把军官的动作安到了 dozens of Indians 头上。 借用原文：The elephant wandered out of the jungle and fell into the well
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：录音说的是大象自己 wandered out of the jungle and fell into the well，是大象游荡，不是这群印度人"发现一头在井边游荡的大象"，选项盗用 wander 和 well 拼出一个原文没说的动作。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（dozens of Indian rescuers rallied together ↔ They gathered together rallied=gathered 同义替换）

questions.evidenceText: It was a heartwarming moment that dozens of Indian rescuers rallied together to use a crane in order to save an elephant trapped at the bottom of a 20-foot well.

questions.stem: Why did the army officers call the local forest department?

options.text: To get food for the elephant.

questions.analysis: 目的题。答案句（P1）：The officers then threw in some food for the creature and called the local forest department for help.信号：for help 点出目的 。答案信号是表目的的 called the local forest department for help 里的 for help——"call... for help"直接说明打电话就…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：crane（起重机）确实在录音里出现过 use a crane，但那是后来营救时用的工具，录音从没说打电话是"为了借起重机"，选项盗用 crane 这个原词制造"听到了就想选"的诱惑。 借用原文：The army officers heard a noise coming from the well
optionAnalysis.C: 答非所问："井里传来奇怪声音"在录音里是军官自己 heard a noise coming from the well，他们打电话是去求助、不是"去报告这个声音"，选项把"听到声音"硬说成打电话的目的。 借用原文：threw in some food for the creature
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱："给大象弄吃的"沾着录音里 threw in some food for the creature，但扔食物是军官自己做的另一件事，不是打电话的目的，选项盗用 food 这个原词来误导。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（called the local forest department for help ↔ To ask them for help for help=ask for help 同义）

questions.evidenceText: The officers then threw in some food for the creature and called the local forest department for help.

questions.stem: What does the news report say happened finally?

options.text: The elephant was able to return to the jungle.
The army officers were examined for injuries.
The army officers were rewarded for their rescue efforts.
The elephant was given medical treatment for many days.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：The elephant was kept under close supervision for a few days before it was successfully released back into the wild.信号：尾句 released 收束结局 。答案信号是录音最后一句的 successfully released back into the wild——"成功放归野外"是整件事的收尾结局，新闻末题答案就在此。

optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴："检查伤情"在录音里有 for evaluation of any injuries，但被检查的是大象，不是"军官"，选项把检查对象从大象偷换成 army officers，听到 injuries 就选会错。 借用原文：kept under close supervision for a few days
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：录音通篇没有说军官因营救"受到奖励"，reward 是凭空添加的情节，属于原文根本没提到的内容。
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：录音说的是 kept under close supervision for a few days（看护了几天），选项却写成 given medical treatment for many days，把"几天看护"夸成"很多天的治疗"，且最终结局是"放归"而非"治疗"，盗用 days 偷改了时长与重点。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（released back into the wild ↔ return to the jungle the wild=the jungle 同义）

questions.evidenceText: The elephant was kept under close supervision for a few days before it was successfully released back into the wild.

transcript.text: M: I need to stop at the bank to withdraw some cash.
transcript.zh: M: 我得去银行取点现金。

transcript.text: W: Why not just pay with your phone?
transcript.zh: W: 为什么不直接用手机支付呢？

transcript.text: M: Well, actually, I've stopped using online payments for the past three months now.
transcript.zh: M: 嗯，实际上，我已经三个月没用线上支付了。

transcript.text: W: Stopped paying online? Oh, you must be worried that online payments aren't secure.
transcript.zh: W: 不用线上支付了？哦，你一定是担心线上支付不安全吧。

transcript.text: M: No, they are safe. But paying online is too convenient and I spent too much money on things I didn't need.
transcript.zh: M: 不，它们是安全的。但线上支付太方便了，我在不需要的东西上花了太多钱。

transcript.text: W: Oh, impulse purchases can be an issue for me, too. I've definitely bought clothes and shoes I didn't need because they were on sale, and paying with my phone was so easy. But I've found that if I review my spending every night, that keeps me from spending too much.
transcript.zh: W: 哦，冲动消费对我来说也是个问题。我确实买过不需要的衣服和鞋子，因为它们在打折，而且用手机支付太容易了。但我发现如果每晚检查一下我的开支，就能控制住不花太多钱。

transcript.text: M: I tried that strategy, but it just didn't work, because I'd be busy studying all day. Then, when I was tired and hungry, I'd use my phone to order food, like burgers and other junk, instead of going to the canteen, where I could get a healthier meal for half the price.
transcript.zh: M: 我试过那个办法，但没用，因为我一整天都在忙着学习。然后，当我又累又饿的时候，我就会用手机点外卖，比如汉堡和其他垃圾食品，而不是去食堂，在那里我可以花一半的价钱吃到更健康的饭菜。

transcript.text: W: Well, what do you do now then? It seems like you'd have the same problems with cash.
transcript.zh: W: 那你现在怎么办呢？感觉你用现金也会有同样的问题啊。

transcript.text: M: I go to the bank once a week, and the rest of the time I keep my bank card at home, so I can't get more cash out. And I also have a notebook where I record my expenses.
transcript.zh: M: 我每周去一次银行，其余时间把银行卡放在家里，这样我就取不到更多现金了。而且我还有个笔记本记录我的开支。

transcript.text: W: But what prevents you from just going to the bank and getting more money, if you want to buy something?
transcript.zh: W: 但如果你想买东西，有什么能阻止你直接去银行取更多钱呢？

transcript.text: M: The first month I did withdraw extra cash twice, but I felt guilty about it. And after that I refused to spend more than what I had budgeted, and by now it's just a habit.
transcript.zh: M: 第一个月我确实又取了两次额外的现金，但我为此感到内疚。之后我就拒绝花超出预算的钱，到现在这已经成了习惯。

questions.stem: Why has the man stopped paying online for the last three months?

options.text: He found it had caused him much inconvenience.
It led him to spend more money than necessary.
It was much less secure than paying with cash.
He wanted to be less dependent on his phone.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P5）：No, they are safe. But paying online is too convenient and I spent too much money on things I didn't need.信号：转折 But 之后才是真因 。男方先用 No, they are safe. 否掉"不安全"的猜测，再用 But 引出真正理由 I spent too much money on things I didn't ne…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：录音说线上付款 too convenient（太方便了），选项却说 caused him much inconvenience（带来很多不便）——A 盗了 convenient 这个原词却反着说，方向正相反。 借用原文：No, they are safe
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：选项 much less secure（不太安全）盗用了"安全"这一话题，但录音明确说 they are safe——他恰恰否认了安全顾虑，C 取的是被否定的方向。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：less dependent on his phone（少依赖手机）听着合理，但录音通篇只说花钱失控，没有一句提到"想摆脱对手机的依赖"，属凭常识硬补。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（I spent too much money on things I didn't need ↔ It led him to spend more money than necessary. "不需要的东西上多花钱"="花了多于必要的钱"）

questions.evidenceText: No, they are safe. But paying online is too convenient and I spent too much money on things I didn't need.

questions.stem: What problem does the woman say she may also have?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：Oh, impulse purchases can be an issue for me, too. I've definitely bought clothes and shoes I didn't need because they were on sale.信号：for me, too 的自我承认 。女方用 can be an issue for me, too（对我来说也是个问题）直接认账，too 是"我也有"的信号，紧接着的 impulse purchases 就是她自陈…

optionAnalysis.A: 过度推断：Living beyond her means（花超过收入）听着像"花太多"，但女方只承认冲动购物，没说自己入不敷出，是程度上的过度引申。
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：Lack of budgeting strategies（缺预算策略）原文无对应；女方反而说自己有 review my spending every night 的办法，谈不上缺策略。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：录音里她提到 bought clothes and shoes，选项 Fashion addiction（迷恋时尚成瘾）借这两个词把"偶尔冲动买"夸成"成瘾"，听到 clothes/shoes 就选会中招。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（impulse purchases can be an issue for me, too ↔ Impulse purchasing. purchases=purchasing，几乎原义对应）

questions.evidenceText: Oh, impulse purchases can be an issue for me, too. I've definitely bought clothes and shoes I didn't need because they were on sale.

questions.stem: What does the man say he could do at the canteen?

options.text: Eat healthier food with less money.
Order food like burgers and chips.
Avoid getting addicted to junk food
Pay either in cash or with his phone.

transcript.text: Lift-off is usually the most environmentally harmful stage of any space mission, with vast quantities of fuel burnt up in a matter of minutes. For instance, SpaceX's Falcon 9 gets through 112 tonnes of refined fuel, emitting about 336 tonnes of CO₂. This is the equivalent produced by your average car driving almost 70 times around the world. As well as greenhouse gases, rocket engines emit particles that destroy ozone. These issues are growing more pressing with the emergence of commercial spaceflight. There were 114 space launches in 2020, but there may be up to 1,000 per year in future.
transcript.zh: 发射通常是任何太空任务中对环境危害最大的阶段,在短短几分钟内燃烧掉大量燃料。例如, SpaceX的猎鹰9号消耗112吨精炼燃料,排放约336吨二氧化碳。这相当于普通汽车绕地球行驶近70圈所产生的排放量。除了温室气体,火箭发动机还排放破坏臭氧的颗粒物。随着商业太空飞行的兴起,这些问题变得越来越紧迫。2020年有114次太空发射,但未来每年可能多达1000次。

transcript.text: Sustainable fuels are the top priority to enable greener space travel. Current spacecraft use a variety of fuels, but most are based on fossil fuels. One potentially greener option is liquid hydrogen and oxygen. Hydrogen can be obtained sustainably by using solar power to break water down into oxygen and hydrogen.
transcript.zh: 可持续燃料是实现更环保太空旅行的首要任务。目前的航天器使用多种燃料,但大多数基于化石燃料。一种潜在的更环保选择是液氢和液氧。氢可以通过利用太阳能将水分解成氧和氢来可持续地获得。

transcript.text: Reusable rockets can cut down on some of the waste associated with spaceflight. Traditionally, boosters, fuel tanks and other components are treated as expendable. But guiding them back to Earth in a controlled manner opens new possibilities — most components from the Falcon 9 can be reused up to 100 times.
transcript.zh: 可重复使用的火箭可以减少与太空飞行相关的一些浪费。传统上,助推器、燃料箱和其他部件被视为一次性消耗品。但以受控方式引导它们返回地球开辟了新的可能性——猎鹰9号的大部分部件可以重复使用多达100次。

transcript.text: Truly environmentally friendly space travel is still some way off. But we already have many of the technologies needed to start limiting its impact on our planet.
transcript.zh: 真正环保的太空旅行仍有一段路要走。但我们已经拥有许多开始限制其对地球影响所需的技术。

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Lift-off is usually the most environmentally harmful stage of any space mission, with vast quantities of fuel burnt up in a matter of minutes.信号：篇章首句即点题 。这是第一段的开篇第一句，篇章独白常把核心论断放在段首；句中 the most environmentally harmful stage"对环境危害最大的阶段"是一个带最高级的明确论断，正是答案句信号。

optionAnalysis.D: It proves to be the most complicated stage of space missions. 盗用了原文的最高级框架 the most environmentally harmful stage，但把 harmful（有害）偷换成 complicated（复杂）。原文讲的是"危害最大"不是"最复杂"，听到 the most…stage 就选，会被这个偷换骗到。

questions.stem: What does the passage say we already have regarding spaceflight?

transcript.text: Helping to look after a pet can facilitate numerous aspects of a child's emotional development. Research shows that reading to a loyal and nonjudgmental companion, such as a dog or cat, can encourage reluctant readers to read aloud, which will in turn boost their self-confidence. Having a companion to talk to about their feelings can also help children feel secure and develop communication skills.
transcript.zh: 帮助照顾宠物可以促进儿童情感发展的诸多方面。研究表明,向忠诚且不评判的伙伴(如狗或猫)朗读可以鼓励不愿意读书的孩子大声朗读,这反过来会增强他们的自信心。有一个可以倾诉感受的伙伴也能帮助儿童感到安全并发展沟通技能。

transcript.text: A household pet can also cultivate a child's sense of responsibility as their parent explains the necessary processes of keeping their pet happy and healthy. As a child matures, they can then take on more of the daily responsibilities, boosting their sense of independence.
transcript.zh: 家庭宠物还可以培养儿童的责任感,因为家长会向他们解释保持宠物快乐和健康的必要过程。随着儿童的成长,他们可以承担更多日常责任,增强独立感。

transcript.text: Pets also provide a fantastic subject for research and learning. Parents can encourage their child to research their favourite pets at the library or during a supervised internet search. Taking children along to the pet shop to buy food and supplies will support their cognitive development as their passion for learning flourishes.
transcript.zh: 宠物还为研究和学习提供了绝佳的主题。家长可以鼓励孩子在图书馆或在监督下的网络搜索中研究他们喜爱的宠物。带孩子去宠物店购买食物和用品将有助于他们的认知发展,因为他们对学习的热情会蓬勃发展。

transcript.text: A child's physical development can benefit greatly from taking pets for walks in the fresh air. Even their fine-motor skills can be utilised in taking care of a beloved animal.
transcript.zh: 带宠物在新鲜空气中散步可以极大地促进儿童的身体发育。甚至他们的精细运动技能也可以在照顾心爱的动物时得到运用。

transcript.text: When responsibilities are well paced and communicated, a child can benefit greatly from involvement in bringing up a happy and healthy pet. And of course, if a child doesn't have a pet in their own household, they can still benefit from all of the above when visiting a friend who does.
transcript.zh: 当责任节奏得当且沟通良好时,儿童可以从参与养育一只快乐健康的宠物中受益匪浅。当然,如果孩子自己家里没有宠物,他们在拜访有宠物的朋友时仍然可以从上述所有方面受益。

transcript.text: A new bill in the Ohio legislature would require state public colleges and universities to send prospective students a packet of information. transcript.zh: 俄亥俄州立法机构的一项新法案将要求州立公立大学和学院向潜在学生发送一份信息包。其中将包括大学费用、助学金和奖学金。还将包括预期的月贷款还款额以及大学毕业后的预期薪资。

transcript.text: State Representative Adam Mathews is one of the two legislators who proposed the bill. He said it would give prospective students more information about what to expect once they graduate. "Putting that information in front of them will give them the best opportunity to match their skills and their dreams to what our schools can provide," said Mathews. He notes that the state can only regulate public institutions in this way, but he hopes private institutions in Ohio follow the lead of the state and post similar information. He believes giving out this information will help Ohio's colleges and universities to be more competitive. The information will highlight what a great value they have for their very reasonable cost.
transcript.zh: 州众议员Adam Mathews是提出该法案的两位立法者之一。他表示，这将为潜在学生提供更多关于毕业后预期情况的信息。Mathews说："将这些信息呈现在他们面前，将使他们有最好的机会将自己的技能和梦想与我们学校所能提供的相匹配。"他指出，州只能以这种方式监管公立机构，但他希望俄亥俄州的私立机构效仿州的做法并发布类似信息。他相信，提供这些信息将有助于俄亥俄州的大学和学院提高竞争力。这些信息将突显出它们以非常合理的成本提供了巨大的价值。

transcript.text: Ohio's schools are already competitive. The state attracts more undergraduate students than it sends to colleges out of state. passages.title: Section B 长篇阅读匹配

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: For all the innovation and choice that define the food and drink industries, if you want to make money, you could do a lot worse than fill a bottle with water and sell it. A litre of tap water, the stuff we have cleverly piped into our homes, costs less than half a penny. A litre of bottled water can cost well over a pound, especially for something fancy that has been sucked through a mountain.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Yet the bottled water market is livelier than ever. It defies our increasing awareness of the harm plastics do to the environment and a broader, growing sense that something has to change. Sales in the UK were worth a record £558.4 million this past year, an increase of 7%, according to the latest figures from the market analyst Kantar. Separate data from other analysts show that last year the British consumed more than 2.2 billion litres of bottled water, including "take-home" and "on-the-go" products. That's an annual rise in volume of 8.5%.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Environmental campaigners are struggling to understand why nations blessed with clean tap water grow only fonder of the bottle. "It's very surprising to me," says Sam Chetan-Walsh, a political adviser at Greenpeace and campaigner against ocean plastic. "Public awareness has never been higher, but the message is not quite reaching all the people it needs to." Where it is heard, the message is causing concern. Plastic water bottles require oceans of fossil fuels to make and ship. Additionally, single-use plastics of all types are polluting our cities and seas. Numerous documentaries have shown how plastic is ultimately killing wildlife.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Moves against various plastics have gathered pace, from shopping bags to straws and plastic-lined coffee cups. Chetan-Walsh argues that bottled water is different because the alternatives are so obvious. "If a product that is so nakedly unnecessary can exist, then the whole system is failing," he says.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Hope is not entirely out of reach. The rate of growth has begun to ease (sales were up 7% in the year, compared with 8% the previous year).

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: But even if large numbers of people are quitting bottled water because of care for the environment, others are taking it up. The introduction of the "sugar tax" on juices and soda drinks has pushed more people to bottled water, while health awareness has boosted its desirability. Tap water consumption is growing at roughly the same pace (UK consumers still drink almost three times as much tap water as bottled water).

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: So the plastic tide only creeps higher. The industry is quick to point out that all its bottles are recyclable. "But collection rates are, at the most generous estimates, 56%, so the actual recycling rate will be lower than that," Chetan-Walsh says. And while bottles may be recyclable, very few are made of recycled plastic. One water bottle company launched recycled half-litre "eco" bottles alongside its standard bottles. Another has pledged to use only recycled plastic across its range by 2025. Chetan-Walsh believes in a ban on single-use bottles. Bans do exist in some places. Organisers of a famous music festival announced that water bottles will not be sold this summer. San Francisco has banned them from city property and events. Last year, the UK government set out plans to ban single-use plastic from its estate.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Water bottlers, unsurprisingly, don't support bans. But they raise concerns about health rather than profit margins. Last month one chief executive of a water bottling company said that bans would "result in greater consumption of sugary drinks, adding to all the health dangers of obesity, diabetes and tooth decay". Kinvara Carey, general manager of an association of the biggest bottled water manufacturers, cites a survey in which people were asked what they would do if bottled water were not available. "Forty-four per cent would buy another drink, which is not great, 14% would go without and 4.5% said they would find a fountain," she says. "The choice is important."

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: What if fountains were more numerous, and tap water more clearly available in cafes, restaurants and elsewhere? Dozens of fountains are being installed in London. There are similar initiatives elsewhere. Before plastic and the marketing that made people think they needed bottled water in the first place, fountains were an urban fixture. Greenpeace, among others, is also pushing for a "deposit return" scheme. This would mean tax on bottled water would be refunded to customers who returned the plastic for recycling.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Even if bottled water sales are growing slightly more slowly, the industry is racing to adapt to changing concerns and tastes. Flavoured water is booming: sales of the sparkling variety shot up by 20%, according to the latest analyst data. Meanwhile, international water brands, as well as a range of new companies, are selling high-end reusable bottles. And if you must fill them with tap water, why not add flavouring?

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: As the owner of multiple sugary drink brands and bottled water, PepsiCo is facing challenges on health and environmental fronts. Last year, the company bought SodaStream (a drinks company that sells machines for making tap water bubbly and then consumers add flavours) for $3.2 billion. It also launched a range of fancy bottles that work with tap water and flavour packets. The bottle is reusable. The packets? Not so much, and, yes, they are made of plastic, although the company invites users to post them back for recycling.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: As is so often the case, clever marketing can beat reason; awareness is rarely enough. "There is always this kind of slip between concern, intent and changed behaviour," says Giles Quick, an analyst of bottled water. "The best example is five a day, the recommendation to have at least five portions of fruit and vegetables every day. Almost everyone is aware of this, but something like 15% of us achieve it." Unless a far-reaching bottle ban does come into force, it will be up to consumers to not only demand change—but to act themselves.
